key_insight: PD-CogT-Sleep will test whether enhancing deep sleep with phase-targeted auditory stimulation improves cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson’s disease and mild cognitive impairment.
clinical_relevance: The study could inform non-drug approaches to cognitive impairment in Parkinson’s disease, but cognitive benefits and disease-modifying effects remain unproven.
method: Single-center, double-blind, randomized sham-controlled trial targeting 50 participants.
Participants receive remotely delivered digital cognitive training plus either auditory stimulation or sham stimulation, allocated 1:1.
Executive function is the primary outcome; additional measures include cognition, participant reports, blood biomarkers, and sleep EEG.
evidence_signal: This design abstract reports planned assessments at baseline, five weeks post-allocation, and three-month follow-up, with no efficacy results.
watch_item: The small, single-center trial may limit generalizability, and biomarker changes alone would not establish slowed disease progression.
paper_title: Enhancing deep sleep with auditory stimulation to boost cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment: Rationale and design of the double-blind randomized controlled trial PD-CogT-Sleep
